pool.text: Jurchen forces under the Jin general Wanyan Wushu crossed the Yangtze and captured Jiankang briefly.
The Hongwu Emperor ascended the throne and established the Ming dynasty in Nanjing.
The Yongle Emperor relocated the capital from Nanjing to his former princedom of Beiping.
The Yingzong Emperor formally dropped Beijing's xingzai prefix, leaving Nanjing as the secondary capital.
More than one million certificates were printed and issued to authorize purchasing salt.
The Zhenwu Regiment mutiny occurred after a sharp spike in rice prices and cuts.
The National Revolutionary Army captured the city during the Northern Expedition.
The Xiaozhuang School founded by Tao Xingzhi was forcibly closed by government order.
A survey showed forty five percent of households lived in shantytowns.
An extreme daily maximum temperature of forty three degrees Celsius occurred.
The city's territory was officially enlarged from 157 to about 466 square kilometres.
A plant began operations producing daily averages of ammonium sulfate and nitric acid.
A Japanese collaborationist government led by Wang Jingwei was established.
The Kuomintang relocated its central government back to Nanjing after Japan surrendered.
Communist forces crossed the Yangtze River and captured Nanjing.
Eighteen hundred projectionists travelled to Nanjing for a special training program.
Nanjing became the capital city of Jiangsu province.
An extreme daily minimum temperature of minus fourteen degrees Celsius occurred.
The massive two tiered road and rail bridge opened to traffic.
Nanjing Railway Station was first built.
